raw_response:
I farm the way I always have to think first about not losing money. Nine mu is not much, and at my age I cannot gamble. Cotton is still my main cash crop, but I keep some land in wheat and maize too. If cotton price is not good, at least grain can carry the house. I do not read those technical papers, I look at my own field and what the other old farmers nearby are doing. Last year if I put too little fertilizer, the crop showed it right away, so this year I will not cut too hard. But fertilizer, water, and medicine all cost cash, so I will not chase fancy yields either.

For the 9 mu, I will keep about 5 mu in cotton, and 4 mu in the wheat-maize rotation. Wheat is already the steady crop here, and after wheat comes off I will put maize in quickly on the same land. Cotton needs more watching and more hand work, but it brings cash if the season is decent. I have a well, so when the crop is really thirsty I can water, but pumping costs money, so I only water at the important times.
